notes: Earlier broad survey is retained with original timestamps; fresh records override its version metadata only when successful.

method_notes: Metadata is an API snapshot. default_version selects the recorded release, not a maximum including older prereleases.
Null rust_version means the crate does not declare it in this metadata; it is not proof of toolchain compatibility.
Metadata SHA-256 fields describe the original raw HTTP responses. This file retains selected fields, not the full raw responses.
README and issue claims are distinguished from source inspection and executed experiments in the report. No search API success-rate or latency benchmark was performed.

upstream_issue_reports.title: Panic with max_extracted_len
Markdown conversion has superlinear output growth for nested HTML tables
upstream_issue_reports.body:
## Reproduction With the PyPI Python package `rs-trafilatura==0.1.1` on macOS / CPython 3.13: ```python import rs_trafilatura def nested(n): inner = "" + "".join( f"" for i in range(n) ) + "
cell{i}acell{i}b
" return f"
{inner}x
" for n in (2, 10, 100, 300): source = nested(n) markdown = rs_trafilatura.html_to_markdown(source) print(n, len(source), len(markdown)) ``` Observed output lengths: | Nested rows | HTML bytes | Markdown bytes | | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 2 | 162 | 284 | | 10 | 474 | 3,732 | | 100 | 4,164 | 343,944 | | 300 | 12,764 | 3,313,846 | The generated Markdown flattens the nested table into the parent cell, then repeatedly pads/alines the resulting table rows. Growth is strongly superlinear, which becomes operationally unsafe for ordinary legacy pages containing deeply or broadly nested tables. ## Impact observed in a batch extraction A public 1,387,515-byte HTML page at https://www2.fmc.gov/FMC1Users/scripts/ExtReports.asp?tariffClass=oti produced 14,816,518,336 bytes of Markdown in 66 seconds with `extract(..., output_markdown=True, include_tables=True, favor_recall=True, include_links=True, include_images=True, include_comments=True)`. The same input produced: - 999,964 characters of plain extracted text with `output_markdown=False, include_tables=True`; - 633,632 characters of Markdown with `output_markdown=True, include_tables=False`. The page parses to a table cell containing a nested table with 9,189 rows and 36,752 descendant cells. This suggests the problem is in nested-table Markdown rendering rather than the base content-selection path. ## Expected behavior Nested tables should either render compactly without repeated width padding, be represented in a bounded fallback form, or have an output-size limit that returns an error rather than allocating an unbounded string. A compact/non-aligned table mode would also avoid whitespace amplification. I can provide additional public-page details or test a candidate fix.

upstream_issue_reports.title: `grab_article` doubles the cloned document's node array on every attempt; running the attempt on `self.doc` avoids it
test: the Rust e2e browser tests leave Chrome running after they exit
upstream_issue_reports.body:
The Rust e2e browser tests leave Chrome processes running after the test binary exits.

## Reproduction

On `integration/0927` at a946422b2 (Linux, Chrome 154):

```
cd e2e/rust
cargo test --release --test browser_test      # 18 passed
for p in $(pgrep chrome); do readlink /proc/$p/cwd; done
```

8 Chrome processes are still running after the tests exit, all with their working directory under `e2e/rust`. The same happens on `deps/html-to-markdown-release` (a10d51e67), so the leak predates that branch.

## Why it matters

On a shared build host the leftover Chrome processes held a browser lock and blocked other test runs for about 30 minutes. #415 covers leaked profile directories; this issue is about the processes.

## Expected

When the e2e test binary exits, no Chrome it started is still running.
